subject.title: wiki_status leaks the existence of another agent's bridged memory artifacts via an unscoped count

question: Should memory-wiki status and doctor report bridge artifact counts scoped to the calling agent, or should global artifact counts remain available only through an explicitly operator-scoped surface?
rationale: The source proves the current count is process-wide, but choosing whether to hide, scope, or split status/doctor semantics changes a security boundary and operator diagnostics behavior.

options.title: Scope agent-visible status
options.body: Thread caller identity into agent-visible `wiki_status` and filter artifacts by `agentIds`, while keeping global counts only behind an explicitly operator-authorized diagnostic path.

options.title: Gate global status
options.body: Treat the count as an operator diagnostic and restrict the exposed status/doctor method so untrusted agent callers cannot invoke it.

options.title: Accept global metadata
options.body: Declare the count intentionally global and accept that agents may infer other agents' bridge artifacts from status output.

recommendation.title: Scope agent-visible status
recommendation.body: Thread caller identity into agent-visible `wiki_status` and filter artifacts by `agentIds`, while keeping global counts only behind an explicitly operator-authorized diagnostic path.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the strongest feature-history and recent validation signal for memory-wiki status, bridge artifacts, and doctor semantics.
